title: Bounded-below flat representatives over the integers
statement: For every $K\in D^+(\mathbf Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] there is a cochain complex $P^\bullet$ of abelian groups, with $P^i=0$ for all $i<b$ for some integer $b$, and an isomorphism $Q(P^\bullet)\cong K$ in $D(\mathbf Z)$. Every $P^i$ is flat over $\mathbf Z$, meaning that $-\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P^i$ preserves short exact sequences of abelian groups. Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; Tag 0653 (more-algebra, lemma-last-one-flat), flatness of the truncation term

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], choose an integer $a$ such that $K$ belongs to $D(\mathbf Z)^{\ge a}$. The representing-complex equivalence in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] supplies a complex $C^\bullet$ of abelian groups with $C^n=0$ for $n<a$ and an isomorphism $Q(C^\bullet)\cong K$. We construct a flat complex mapping quasi-isomorphically to this $C^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; explicit elementary construction written here

proof.text: For $n\ge a$ let $A_n$ be the group of finitely supported functions from the underlying set of $C^n$ to $\mathbf Z$, with pointwise addition, and let $e_n:A_n\to C^n$ send $\lambda$ to $\sum_{c\in C^n}\lambda(c)c$. For $n<a$ set $A_n=0$ and $e_n=0$. Each $e_n$ is surjective: for $n\ge a$ the function supported at $c$ with value $1$ maps to $c$, and below $a$ the target is zero. Each $A_n$ is torsion free since an equation $m\lambda=0$ with nonzero integer $m$ gives $m\lambda(c)=0$ in $\mathbf Z$ at every coordinate, hence $\lambda=0$.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; explicit elementary construction written here

proof.text: Define $F^n=A_n\oplus A_{n-1}$, $d_F^n(x,y)=(0,x)$, and $q^n(x,y)=e_n(x)+d_C^{n-1}e_{n-1}(y)$. Then $d_F^{n+1}d_F^n=0$ and $q^{n+1}d_F^n(x,y)=d_C^n e_n(x)=d_C^nq^n(x,y)$, so $q:F^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ is a chain map. It is surjective in every degree because $e_n$ is, and $F^n=0$ for $n<a$. Each $F^n$ is torsion free, coordinatewise in its two summands.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; explicit elementary construction written here

proof.text: Let $G^n=\ker q^n\subseteq F^n$. The chain-map identity makes $d_F$ restrict to a differential $d_G$ on $G$, and the inclusions $i^n:G^n\to F^n$ form a chain map. Use the cone formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to define $P^n=F^n\oplus G^{n+1}$ and $d_P^n(f,g)=(d_F^n f+i^{n+1}g,-d_G^{n+1}g)$. Explicitly, $d_P^{n+1}d_P^n(f,g)=(d_F^{n+1}d_F^n f+d_F^{n+1}i^{n+1}g-i^{n+2}d_G^{n+1}g,d_G^{n+2}d_G^{n+1}g)=(0,0)$ because $d_F i=i d_G$. The maps $p^n:P^n\to C^n$, $p^n(f,g)=q^n(f)$, form a chain map since $qi=0$. If $n<a-1$, both $F^n$ and $G^{n+1}$ are zero, so $P^n=0$.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; explicit elementary construction written here

proof.text: The map $p$ is surjective on every cohomology group. Indeed, let $c\in C^n$ be a cycle and lift it to $f\in F^n$ using the surjectivity of $q^n$. Then $q^{n+1}(d_F f)=d_Cc=0$, so $d_F f\in G^{n+1}$. The element $(f,-d_F f)\in P^n$ is a cycle: its first differential component is $d_F f-d_F f=0$ and its second is $d_F^2 f=0$. Its image under $p$ is $c$.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; explicit elementary construction written here

proof.text: The map $p$ is injective on every cohomology group. Suppose $(f,g)\in P^n$ is a cycle and $p(f,g)=d_C c_0$ for some $c_0\in C^{n-1}$. Lift $c_0$ to $t\in F^{n-1}$ using $q^{n-1}(t)=c_0$ and subtract the boundary $d_P(t,0)$ from $(f,g)$. Writing $f_1=f-d_F^{n-1}t$, we have $q^n f_1=p(f,g)-d_C^{n-1}q^{n-1}t=d_C^{n-1}c_0-d_C^{n-1}c_0=0$, so the resulting cycle $(f_1,g)$ has $f_1\in G^n$. Its cycle equation is $d_G f_1+g=0$. Hence $(f_1,g)=(i f_1,-d_G f_1)=d_P^{n-1}(0,f_1)$ is a boundary, where $(0,f_1)\in F^{n-1}\oplus G^n=P^{n-1}$. Thus the original cycle is a boundary too. Together with the preceding step and the definition of quasi-isomorphism in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], this proves that $p$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant), first model-construction paragraph; explicit elementary construction written here

proof.text: Every $G^n$ is torsion free: if $mg=0$ with $m\ne0$, its image in the torsion-free group $F^n$ is zero, so $g=0$. Therefore every $P^n=F^n\oplus G^{n+1}$ is torsion free as well. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] to the principal ideal domain $\mathbf Z$ (the zero ideal is generated by $0$; a nonzero ideal is generated by its least positive element, by division with remainder) and the $\mathbf Z$-module $P^n$ for each $n$. It follows that each $P^n$ is flat, with no finite-generation hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (1), with the explicit subgroup and direct-sum checks above

proof.text: To verify the exact meaning of flatness requested here, fix $n$ and a short exact sequence $0\to U\to V\to W\to0$ of abelian groups. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] with $R=\mathbf Z$ and $M=P^n$ to each of the exact triples $0\to U\to V$, $U\to V\to W$ and $V\to W\to0$. Since $0\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P^n=0$ (every elementary tensor with zero is zero), these give injectivity at the left, exactness at the middle and surjectivity at the right of the tensored sequence. Thus $-\otimes_{\mathbf Z}P^n$ preserves short exact sequences.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat): flatness is equivalent to exactness of the tensor functor

proof.text: By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], localization sends the quasi-isomorphism $p:P^\bullet\to C^\bullet$ to an isomorphism $Q(p):Q(P^\bullet)\to Q(C^\bullet)$. Composing this map with the step-1 isomorphism $Q(C^\bullet)\cong K$ gives the required isomorphism $Q(P^\bullet)\cong K$. The lower bound $b=a-1$ from step 4 and the flatness and short-exact-sequence preservation from steps 7 and 8 give every clause of the statement.
